verdict: Roblox grew revenue 36% to $1.47B as more than 120 million daily users played over 29 billion hours, but bookings growth slowed to 8% — players spent less per hour — and it still lost $185M.

kpis.label: Bookings
kpis.note: +8% YoY — the cash players actually spent

segments.name: Platform revenue
segments.note: Sales of Robux (the platform's virtual currency) and subscriptions, recognized gradually over the ~27 months players are expected to keep spending. The cash collected upfront ('bookings') was $1,557M.

opex.name: Developer exchange fees
opex.note: The cut paid out to creators when players spend Robux in their games — Roblox raised creator pay rates in September 2025.

opex.name: Infrastructure and trust & safety
opex.note: Servers and computing (including AI) plus the safety operation that polices the platform.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform, tools and AI features.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference. Costs ran to $112.60 per $100 of revenue — the extra is the loss, covered by cash the company already had.

takeaways.title: The audience kept growing
takeaways.text: Daily active users passed 120 million and hours engaged topped 29 billion in the quarter — reach is not the problem.

takeaways.title: Bookings slowed sharply
takeaways.text: Bookings — Robux cash sales — grew only 8%, landing at the low end of guidance: a discovery-algorithm change that favors retention cut spending per hour, especially among younger U.S. and Canadian players.

takeaways.title: Losses, but cash-positive
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was +$294M despite the $185M accounting loss: players pay upfront, and $282M of the quarter's costs were stock pay, not cash.

oneTimers: Revenue is not the cash in: bookings were $1,557M but revenue was $1,469M. Roblox defers most bookings and recognizes them over the 27-month average paying-user lifetime, so reported revenue lags the cash by design.
Roblox bought back about $380M of its own shares in the quarter under a new $3B repurchase program announced in May 2026 — a use of cash, not an expense in the figures above.
otherDetail: Interest and other items netted +$46M: $59M of interest earned on Roblox's investment pile, minus $10M of interest expense and $3M of other expense.
